A Foreword is a short introduction to the book, usually by a person other than the author. The purpose of the Foreword is to introduce the author or his/her work.
A Foreword could talk about why the book’s content is relevant in its current scenario or how it created a historical impact when it was first released or the importance of the author’s work.

The Foreword is usually signed by its writer with his/her credentials and the date. You can delete this page if you do not wish to include a Foreword in the book.

A Prologue, in case of fiction books, can be an excerpt from the book or a section of the story that happens before the true beginning of the story. It could provide readers an introduction to the nature of the characters in the story, a view of events that happened earlier and also set the tone of the book.
An Introduction, in case of non-fiction books, defines what the book is about, what a reader can expect from the book, the motivation for the book and, sometimes, guidance on how to use the book.

The house at the end of Black Hollow Lane had been empty for years, yet every night a single lamp glowed behind its cracked windows. No one remembered who built it, only that screams once echoed there and were never answered. When Arjun inherited the property, curiosity outweighed fear. On his first night inside, the walls whispered his name, softly at first, then with growing urgency.

As midnight struck, the temperature dropped sharply. Footsteps echoed above him, slow and deliberate, though the upper floor had collapsed decades ago. In the mirror across the hallway, a shadow appeared behind him—tall, faceless, and breathing. When Arjun turned, nothing was there, but the mirror now showed him smiling… though he wasn’t.

Unable to sleep, Arjun searched the house records and found a single line repeated on every page: The house does not let go. At dawn, he tried to leave, but the front door led back into the hallway. The whispers returned, louder now, pleading for company.

By nightfall, the lamp still burned. Neighbors passing by swore they saw two figures standing at the window—one watching the road, the other trapped behind the glass, screaming silently to be let out.

Video provides a powerful way to help you prove your point. When you click Online Video, you can paste in the embed code for the video you want to add. You can also type a keyword to search online for the video that best fits your document.

To make your document look professionally produced, Word provides header, footer, cover page, and text box designs that complement each other. For example, you can add a matching cover page, header, and sidebar. Click Insert and then choose the elements you want from the different galleries.

Themes and styles also help keep your document coordinated. When you click Design and choose a new Theme, the pictures, charts, and SmartArt graphics change to match your new theme. When you apply styles, your headings change to match the new theme.

Save time in Word with new buttons that show up where you need them. To change the way a picture fits in your document, click it and a button for layout options appears next to it. When you work on a table, click where you want to add a row or a column, and then click the plus sign.
Reading is easier, too, in the new Reading view. You can collapse parts of the document and focus on the text you want.
If you need to stop reading before you reach the end, Word remembers where you left off - even on another device.

The house stood alone at the edge of the village, its windows dark and unblinking. Locals avoided it after sunset, claiming it remembered every voice that entered. When Ravi arrived, dust covered the floors, yet the air felt strangely warm, as if someone had just left. The door closed behind him without a sound, sealing the silence inside.

That night, the walls began to murmur. At first it was only fragments—broken words drifting through the corridors. Ravi pressed his ear against the plaster and heard breathing on the other side. When he spoke, the house answered, repeating his words in a slower, distorted voice that did not sound human.

In the hallway mirror, Ravi noticed his reflection moving a second too late. The face stared back with hollow eyes and a smile stretched too wide. He reached out to touch the glass, and cold fingers pressed back from inside, leaving dark handprints that slowly bled down the surface.

By morning, the villagers saw the lights return to the house. Ravi was never seen again. Sometimes, when the wind is right, his voice can be heard whispering warnings to those who pass—begging them not to listen.

When Karthik inherited the old ancestral house, no one congratulated him. The villagers only lowered their eyes and warned him never to sleep on the ground floor. The wooden boards creaked even when no one walked on them, and at night, the house exhaled a damp, rotten breath that carried the smell of soil and decay.

On the third night, scratching began beneath the floorboards. It was slow, deliberate, as if fingernails were searching for a way out. Karthik lifted a loose plank and found deep claw marks carved into the wood from below. When he replaced it, the scratching stopped—only to resume directly beneath his bed.

At the end of the corridor stood a door sealed with rusted chains. Family records mentioned it only once: Do not open after sunset. Driven by fear and curiosity, Karthik broke the lock at midnight. Inside, the walls were covered with names—some freshly carved, still bleeding.

A voice rose from beneath the room, whispering his name with perfect familiarity. The floor collapsed, dragging him into darkness. By morning, the house was silent again, waiting patiently for its next inheritance.
